description: This event is in-person only, but open to UCSF clinicians, researchers, and educators. This talk presents Mindfulness-Based Health Promotion (MBHP), a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) developed in Brazil and culturally adapted to Brazilian public policies. Drawing on more than a decade of work at the Mente Aberta Center (Federal University of São Paulo), the talk traces the cultural aspects of these practices in Brazil, their adaptation to Brazilian public policies, especially to our national health system (SUS), and the evidence supporting MBHP's effectiveness as a public policy tool for supported self-care and health equity. The presentation also reflects on the speaker's own relationship to contemplative practice and its integration with preventive and lifestyle medicine. Marcelo Demarzo, MD, PhD, is a physician specializing in Family Medicine, Sports Medicine, Preventive Medicine, and Lifestyle Medicine, and an expert (teacher, trainer and researcher) in secular, evidence-based mindfulness and compassion training. He is Associate Professor (Livre-Docente) at the Federal University of São Paulo (UNIFESP), Senior Fellow in Primary Health Care at the University of Oxford, and Visiting Researcher at UTS Sydney, the University of Melbourne, Universidad de Zaragoza, and Macau University of Science and Technology. He is a CNPq Research Productivity Fellow and holds a PhD in Experimental Pathology. In 2011 he founded the Mente Aberta Center at UNIFESP and developed the Mindfulness-Based Health Promotion (MBHP) protocol, now widely implemented across the Brazilian public health system (SUS). He is the Executive Director of CABSIN (Brazilian Academic Consortium for Integrative Health), a collaborative network of over 300 affiliated researchers advancing evidence-based Traditional, Complementary, and Integrative Medicine and informing Brazilian public health policy. He also serves as a consultant to the World Health Organization and is a global reference in mindfulness, supported self-care, and health promotion research. The Osher Center for Integrative Health hosts monthly research seminars that are open to the research and clinical community at large. Seminars are held from September to June and are generally virtual. Presentations cover a wide range of topics relating to integrative health, many with a focus on integrative health equity. Research Seminars are organized by Ariana Thompson-Lastad, PhD and Joanne Qina’au, PhD, MA, E-YT750. description: What’s new in PacBio HiFi sequencing, and how can the latest advances help researchers generate deeper biological insights? Join us for a Lunch & Learn with PacBio exploring the latest developments in HiFi sequencing, including new chemistry, RNA sequencing applications, and bioinformatics tools designed to simplify analysis and expand research capabilities. The session will highlight SPRQ-Nx chemistry, including its potential to deliver significant cost savings while maintaining the advantages of HiFi sequencing. Attendees will also learn about advances in Kinnex RNA-seq and recent research from the Tabula Sapiens Consortium exploring transcript isoform diversity. The presentation will also cover new bioinformatics tools designed to streamline data analysis and help researchers unlock deeper biological insights from their sequencing data. Noelle Bittner, Ph.D., Sequencing Specialist at PacBio, and Matt Hestand, Ph.D., Field Bioinformatics Manager at PacBio, will discuss the latest PacBio technologies and applications, with a focus on how these advances can support a range of genomics and transcriptomics research workflows. The session will conclude with an opportunity for questions and discussion about PacBio HiFi sequencing, Kinnex RNA-seq, and bioinformatics applications. Enjoy a complimentary lunch while connecting with colleagues and learning about the latest advances in PacBio sequencing technologies. Seats are limited. Reserve your spot today: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=SjmSTFxSGk2CZ5NhDCTceTXExU_77q5MkYLjziS4HsJUM0xRTFJKMjlaVU5BNkEzRVowMDFWOURJWS4u We encourage you to share this invitation with colleagues and collaborators who may be interested. We look forward to seeing you!

description: This month we are joined by Kelly Yoo and Meenu Krishnakumar from Stanford, who will discuss their work on MySuppleHub. Over half of US adults use dietary supplements, yet the evidence supporting many products remains fragmented, uneven in quality, and often influenced by industry funding. MySuppleHub, developed by the Snyder Lab in the Department of Genetics at Stanford, approaches this problem as an open science opportunity. The platform combines a citation-linked supplement encyclopedia with community surveys, polls, and self-reported experiences, creating a shared evidence base in which participants can both contribute their experiences and benefit from a growing body of accessible, evidence-informed information. The Bay Area Open Science Group is a growing community for Bay Area academics and researchers interested in incorporating open science into their research, teaching, and learning. Targeting students, faculty, and staff at UCSF, Berkeley, and Stanford, the goal of the community is to increase awareness of and engagement with all things open science, including open access articles, open research data, open source software, and open educational resources. Through this work the group hopes to connect researchers with tools they can use to make the products and process of science more equitable and reproducible.

description: What helps people feel that they truly belong—and what happens when they do?
